name: Adshares
rootCause: The Wrapped ADS (wADS) bridge token exposed a wrapTo(account, amount, from, txid) minting function callable by the bridge minter address, but the contract performed no on-chain validation that the supplied from/txid corresponded to a genuine, finalized native-chain lock/burn event. With the minter privilege (or via a compromised/abusable minter path), the attacker invoked wrapTo three times with fabricated native-chain from and txid values to mint ~120M wADS to themselves with no real backing deposit on the Adshares native chain. Because the minter's mint allowance was simply decremented without any cryptographic proof of the corresponding source-chain transaction, the bridge accepted forged mints, allowing ~$628K of value to be drained. Adshares Bridge was exploited on Ethereum around May 15, 2026. The attacker used the bridge-minter EOA to sign three wrapTo() calls with non-existent native-chain transaction IDs on the Adshares canonical chain. This allowed minting large amounts of fake wrapped ADS (wADS: 99,999.93 ×2 + 999,999.94). The fake tokens were then dumped via Uniswap V4 UniversalRouter, draining roughly $628K in ETH and USDC from liquidity pools. Security researchers flagged it quickly, and the project posted an on-chain whitehat message offering a 10% bounty for return of 90% of funds.

On 15 May 2026, the Adshares bridge on Ethereum Mainnet was exploited via forged native-chain transaction IDs, resulting in unauthorized minting of Wrapped ADS tokens worth over $628,000. The attacker sold most of these tokens for ETH and USDC before partial funds were reportedly returned. The bridge contract failed to verify that submitted native-chain transaction IDs corresponded to legitimate deposits, allowing the attacker to mint unbacked tokens by fabricating transaction identifiers.
